rows.title_brief: Randomized controlled trial about the impact of oral antimicrobial prophylaxis on surgical site infection in laparoscopic colorectal surgery
rows.title_acronym: RCT of oral antimicrobial prophylaxis in laparoscopic colorectal surgery
rows.scientific_title: Randomized controlled trial about the impact of oral antimicrobial prophylaxis on surgical site infection in laparoscopic colorectal surgery
rows.scientific_title_acronym: RCT of oral antimicrobial prophylaxis in laparoscopic colorectal surgery
rows.condition: Patients undergoing elective laparoscopic colorectal surgery
rows.narrative_objectives: The aim of this prospective randomized controlled trial was to compare the efficacy of a combination of oral and intravenous antibiotics with intravenous antibiotics alone on the incidence of surgical site infection in patients undergoing elective laparoscopic colorectal surgery.
rows.primary_outcomes: The primary endpoint is the incidence of overall surgical site infection.
rows.key_secondary_outcomes: The secondary endpoints are the incidence of incisional site infections, organ/space infections, and enterocolitis.
rows.institution_consideration: Institution is not considered as adjustment factor.
rows.interventions_control_1: Patients assigned to the non-Oral group received 1 g of cefmetazole intravenously 30 min before the skin incision, then every 3 h during and immediately after the operation, stopping 24 h after completion of surgery.
rows.interventions_control_2: Patients assigned to the Oral group received 750 mg of metronidazole and 1000 mg of kanamycin orally at 15:00 and 21:00 on the day before the surgery in addition to the same antibiotic regimen as the patients in the non-Oral group.
rows.key_inclusion_criteria:
Patients undergoing elective laparoscopic colorectal surgery
Patients who inderstand the study and agre with written informed consent.
rows.key_exclusion_criteria:
1)ileus
2)synchronous resection of other major organs
3)Patients who need antibiotics for other infectious diseases.
4)Patients who have undergone antibiotic administration 2 weeks before the surgery.
5)Patients with severe liver dysfunction
6)Patients with severe renal impairment
7)Patients with severe cardiac dysfunction
8)Patients with severe pulmonary dysfunction
9)Pregnancy or suspicion of pregnancy
10)lactating women
11)Patients who are considered unsuitable for the doctor
